learn.title: Networking: VNets, subnets, peering, DNS, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, endpoints
objectives: Describe what Azure virtual networks and subnets do: isolation, segmentation, communication and filtering.
Explain VNet peering, including global peering over the Microsoft backbone.
Describe Azure DNS and what it does and doesn't do.
Compare VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute for connecting on-premises networks.
concepts: Virtual network (VNet)
A private, isolated network in Azure. You define its address space, and resources in it can talk to each other, to the internet, and to on-premises networks.
Subnet
A range of addresses inside a VNet, used to segment resources (for example web tier and database tier).
Network security group (NSG)
Rules that allow or deny inbound and outbound traffic to subnets or network interfaces.
VNet peering
Connects two VNets so traffic flows privately over the Microsoft backbone. Global peering links VNets in different regions. No gateway required.
Azure DNS
Hosts DNS domains in Azure using Microsoft's global name servers. You can't buy domain names from it. Private DNS zones resolve names inside VNets.
VPN Gateway
Sends encrypted traffic over the public internet. Site-to-site (office to Azure), point-to-site (single device to Azure) and VNet-to-VNet.
ExpressRoute
A private connection to Microsoft's network through a connectivity provider. Traffic doesn't cross the public internet; offers predictable performance and can reach Microsoft 365.
ExpressRoute Global Reach
Links on-premises sites to each other through their ExpressRoute circuits.
Public endpoint
An address reachable from the internet.
Private endpoint
A network interface with a private IP from your VNet that connects privately to a service through Azure Private Link.
comparisons: VPN: encrypted, over the internet, quick and cheaper. ExpressRoute: private circuit, more reliable and predictable, higher bandwidth, costs more and needs a provider.
Site-to-site connects a whole office network. Point-to-site connects one device.
Peering uses the Microsoft backbone with low latency and no gateway. VNet-to-VNet VPN uses gateways and encrypted tunnels.
Public: reachable over the internet. Private: a private IP inside your VNet, traffic stays off the public internet.
traps: Azure DNS doesn't let you buy domain names; you register them elsewhere and host them in Azure DNS.
ExpressRoute traffic isn't encrypted by default just because it is private.
Peering isn't transitive: A-B and B-C peering doesn't connect A to C.
Subnets segment a VNet; they don't connect VNets together.
Point-to-site is for individual devices, not whole offices.
revision: VNet = isolation and communication. Subnet = segmentation. NSG = filtering.
Peering = private, backbone, no gateway, regional or global.
VPN Gateway = encrypted over internet. ExpressRoute = private, not over internet.
Azure DNS = host zones, not buy domains.
Private endpoint = private IP for a PaaS service in your VNet.
